sources.title: Query-wise binary CE and gradient denominators
sources.details: Image gaps are 1.9,1.4 and text gaps 1.6,1.7. Per query CE=log(1+exp(-gap)); each direction averages two queries. Direction gradients are (softmax_rows(S)-I)/2 and (softmax_cols(S)-I)/2; final gradient averages these. The 2:1 weighted loss uses denominator 3 and gradient (2*Gi+Gt)/3. Loss units nats; scores dimensionless. Details independently computed and finite-differenced in audit.py.

claims.statement: With image rows and text columns, image queries classify over text columns; transposing makes text the queries and image rows the candidates. Diagonal [0,1] labels encode the two aligned pairs, and the two-direction mean is a symmetric paired contrastive objective.
claims.scope: Hand-set 2x2 paired table with exactly one declared positive per query; not a general rule that all datasets have diagonal positives or that arbitrary similarities already are probabilities.

evidence.locator: §2.2, PDF p.3, Figure 3: [n,n] logits, labels arange(n), axis=0/1 CE and loss=(loss_i+loss_t)/2
evidence.supports: Original paired-batch symmetric objective. Its pseudocode axis names were mapped independently to PyTorch class dimension rather than copied as direction labels.
Candidates are class dimension 1, values are logits, and default reduction averages queries.
For the 2D scores tensor, .T reverses the two axes.

claims.statement: The asymmetric table produces directional mean CE 0.1799 and 0.1758, overall mean 0.1779 and gradient signs [[-1,1],[1,-1]]; differing row and column competitors make the directional losses unequal.
claims.scope: Two candidates and two queries per direction, equal direction weights, natural-log units; numbers and signs concern this fixed table.

evidence.supports: Independent log1p exponential arithmetic, correct query and direction denominators and analytic gradient.
Unchanged float32 fence reproduces all rounded values and signs.
Float64 values 0.17990208410070582, 0.1758433851373024, 0.1778727346190041; finite differences confirm shared gradient.

verification.expected: Directional query means and their mean match the manuscript at four decimal places; negative diagonal/positive off-diagonal gradient.
verification.details: No pre-softmax input; each directional mean divides by 2 queries, then direction mean divides by 2. Direction probability sums checked along rows/columns; symmetric-table variant gives equal directional losses.
verification.tolerance: Rounded manuscript losses ±0.00005; float64 analytic comparison 1e-14; finite differences eps=1e-6, absolute tolerance 1e-9.

claims.scope: One scalar backward on a 2D leaf score tensor in the existing CPU .venv. It calculates gradients without updating scores or training image/text encoders. APIs and ordinary Python output syntax are covered as one related group.

claims.statement: Selecting among existing candidate cards is distinct from generating a caption; paired contrastive features alone do not prove generation ability. If more than one candidate is genuinely correct, a single-index target can create false negatives and the positive-pair rule must reflect that.
claims.scope: Conceptual task/evidence distinction and conditional ambiguity of one-positive classification; the lesson does not implement or claim to verify a multi-positive loss or caption model.

evidence.locator: §2.2 PDF pp.2–3: caption-prediction model versus proxy predicting which whole text is paired; Figure 3 diagonal labels
evidence.supports: Original paper explicitly distinguishes exact-text prediction from paired whole-text selection, while permitting learned image/text features.
One class-index target identifies one correct class in the candidate set; this API does not infer alternate semantic positives.
Two identical-score candidates with diagonal targets give log(2)=0.69314718056 and positive off-diagonal gradients, exposing rejection under the declared single-positive rule.
Historical experiment selects among six label/image candidates; no free-form generation evaluation is present.

factual_accuracy.details: Six substantive groups cover axes/objective, arithmetic, related API/action, weighted exercise, historical comparison, task distinction/positive-pair limits. Original authority and implementation contracts independently read; no legacy report or author correction summary was used.

numeric_verification.details: Independent query-wise nat arithmetic, explicit 2 queries/2 candidates/2 direction denominators, double-precision analytic and finite-difference gradient, weighted denominator 3, and raw historical sample/query counts were checked.

figure_consistency.details: No figure is referenced in 10.11. The explicit 2x2 matrix and paired candidate numbers supply correspondence. Actual desktop/mobile section rendering was viewed, including horizontally scrolled mobile code; displayed code matched the original fence. Original paper Figure 3 was also rendered and viewed.

source_verification.details: Direct publisher CLIP PDF and official PyTorch v2.9.0 release originals fetched and inspected at concrete locators; dates, URLs and hashes retained. Installed CPU 2.14.1 is explicitly distinguished. Source indexes were locator-only; official HTML HTTP 403 did not prevent original-source contract verification.

limitations.details: The fence calculates gradients without updating or using encoders; historical measurements are one finite synthetic six-candidate run, read-only reconciled rather than retrained or re-inferred. No GPU, model/data download, saved neural checkpoint, paid computation or caption-capability test occurred. Equal six-query counts show no observed advantage here and provide no universal retrieval theorem. This independent technical review is neither a first-reading session nor human learner validation.
